policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV explicitly reads the personal name 'Bani,' distinguishing the qere/base reading from ketiv Benjamin.

ASV's 'were free from other service' conveys the contextual sense but does not distinguish the qere spelling/vocalization from the ketiv; no mapped textual note decides the reading, so the base fallback is retained.
